correctness_confidence.basis: Rigorously verified across 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems without axioms or sorries, paired with an exact AST-audited pure-integer finite-field verification engine.

rigor.basis: Impeccable mathematical and formal verification standards, featuring exact closed-form defect factorizations, universal skew-norm cocycle identities, and strict rank profile bounds.

novelty.basis: First formal machine-checked analysis of Overbeck-LRS Frobenius-shift bounds, public-key invariance, and shortening block-collapse criteria for multi-block linearized Reed-Solomon codes.

significance.basis: Resolves fundamental security and structural properties of post-quantum McEliece candidates based on multi-block LRS codes following recent cryptanalytic breakthroughs by Astore et al.

reproducibility.basis: Exemplary artifact availability with explicit SHA-256 hashes for Lean proofs, Python verification engine, and 16 finite-field certificates verified via 93 adversarial pytest checks.

summary: This manuscript presents a machine-checked, zero-float finite-field verification and algebraic cryptanalysis suite (LRS-STRUCT-RECOV-CERT-1.0) formalizing Overbeck-LRS Frobenius-shift distinguishers, skew-polynomial norm identities, and shortening block-collapse criteria for Linearized Reed-Solomon (LRS) codes in Lean 4.36.0 and an exact Python engine.
strengths: Comprehensive formalization of 20 core theorems in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorries and zero Classical.choice, establishing utmost mathematical certainty.
Exact closed-form factorization of the Overbeck-LRS rank defect delta_LRS = (t + 1 - l)(k - l), explicitly proving onset at t = l and public-key invariance.
Rigorous shortening-block collapse criterion demonstrating how high-rate LRS codes collapse off-primary blocks to force single-step Overbeck distinguishers.
Extensive finite-field verification suite featuring 16 SHA-256 indexed certificates audited by 93 adversarial pytest checks across diverse extension fields.
weaknesses: The complete end-to-end polynomial-time parameter-recovery algorithm of Astore et al. and general MSRD duality theory are imported from literature rather than re-proved inside Lean.
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal skew-norm cocycle N_{i+j}(a) = N_i(a) sigma^i(N_j(a)) and Frobenius shift law proven constructively for arbitrary multiplicative endomorphisms.
Exact closed-form Overbeck-LRS Frobenius-sum bound and defect factorization proving structural onset behavior for multi-block LRS codes.
Shortening-induced block-collapse theorem proving exact dimension bounds for residual blocks and enabling single-step distinguishers in high-rate regimes.
